column1: # Exact stock -> fork identity rewrites for the termux-tools package (helpers, login, conffile).
# Canonical table: it is read by TermuxHelperRewrites (bootstrap extraction) and rendered into
# $PREFIX/libexec/termuxpp/helper-rewrites.tsv for the APT post-invoke hook (adapt-helpers), so the
# installer and the hook can never disagree.
# Row kinds (tab separated), applied in this order to every file they name:
#   identity <stock text> <fork text>            literal replace in every text file of termux-tools
#   rule     <file> <stock text> <fork text>     literal replace in one named file
#   append   <file> <marker> <text>              append text unless the marker is already in the file;
#                                                \n in the text is a newline
#   require  <file> <text> <guard>               hook only: the adapted file must contain the text
#   forbid   <file> <text> <guard>               hook only: the adapted file must not contain the text
#                                                (the guard is @FORK_ONLY@, so that the checks vanish for
#                                                the stock identity, and a failed check makes the hook fail)
# the name of the environment variable that holds the path of the native pkg-redirect library and
# @CONFIG_DIR_NAME@ the canonical config directory relative to the home directory (.config/termuxpp). They
# and @FORK_ONLY@ are empty for the stock identity, so those rows are dropped and stock stays byte-identical. A row with an
# unresolved placeholder, or one that would change nothing, is ignored.
# Rules are literal, never patterns. Java class names stay under com.termux.* and are deliberately not
# rewritten. Every stock text is chosen so that the fork text never matches it again (idempotent).
# The path of the pkg-redirect library is never written down: scripts only reference the variable.
# The login rows look up motd.sh and shell in ~/.config/termuxpp, ~/.config/termux and ~/.termux, in that
# order (the first existing one wins), spelled with $HOME so that the stock text ~/.termux/... never
# The motd rows address single stock lines of etc/motd (\n in a rule text is a newline, so that a rule can
# remove a line): a motd the user edited keeps its own text, only the recognisable stock lines are rewritten.
# There are deliberately no require or forbid rows for the motd, a custom motd must never fail the hook.
# The stock profile script init-termux-properties.sh copies an example termux.properties into ~/.termux when
# there is none in the two stock places, which would put a stale second copy next to the one in
# ~/.config/termuxpp. The rows add the canonical file to the condition and make the example go there; the
# last one also skips the example once config.yaml exists (the app migrates the example to it). They
# are written without tabs (tabs separate the fields) and without the data directory (only fixed text).

column4: for termuxpp_motd in "$HOME/@CONFIG_DIR_NAME@/motd.sh" "$HOME/.config/termux/motd.sh" "$HOME/.termux/motd.sh"; do if [ -f "$termuxpp_motd" ]; then break; fi; done; if [ -f "$termuxpp_motd" ]; then
